doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Defiance, yin and yang, and the period after 1972
summary: He says his defiance affected his sound and relates other breakthroughs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yeah. I was gung ho. In fact, I’d blow two or three choruses and do this.
I was defiant. And hey, that’s easy to be.

Sure, yeah. I mean, you want to fight? Well, you can’t play music like that. It comes out in your music. You’re growling and all that other stuff. So once I was around my daughter for three months, I said, whew. I said, “Girl.” She said, “You’re about to get to be a preacher, aren’t you?”
So this is another one of these breakthroughs that you made.

You were talking – actually, before the tape, before we changed tape, we were talking about the period between ’72 and ’76. Remember we were talking about that, after that album you did with Rahsaan? You were saying that you developed – you felt like you made some deeper developments during that period. That’s another thing.

Sure, because it’s all really your soul that you’re getting in contact with. Like as far as my little meager knowledge goes, it’s there, and you have to try to discover it. We all do. So that’s just, hey.
